account: It is day 0, just after ten, and I am at the plaza for my scheduled market walk. So far I have no evidence of anything unusual in town: Townsfolk 10, 20, and 30 each told me they had no news. This morning there was a small administrative mix-up. I took the appointment book from the office chest to read it; the secretary later found the chest empty and asked whether I had the book and what today's schedule was. I returned it and told the secretary my appointments, then saw the secretary take it from the chest. The secretary has now followed me to the plaza carrying a writable book, presumably to coordinate the day's business, although I have not heard an explanation. I heard the secretary speaking while I was walking away from the office but could not make out the words. I have asked again which east-bank dockside cottage hosts my three o'clock tea and whether correspondence needs attention. Those details remain unconfirmed. My remaining appointments today are lunch at home at noon, office accounts at one, tea at three, back to the office at four thirty, and home at seven. Tomorrow's ten o'clock appointment is a grain inspection at the mill.
